jobs.title: Director, Customer Operations Vendor Strategy & Execution
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

We're looking for a senior leader to join the Affirm Global Operations team as the Director, Vendor Strategy & Operations
to lead Affirm's global BPO and vendor operations program and serve as a true partner in reinventing how we serve customers at scale across our large global vendor network. This leader owns the customer operations vendor strategy, performance, and outcomes of our global servicing network vendor program — customer experience, compliance, operational excellence, resiliency, and cost-to-serve — across a rapidly growing and complex business. The role will be taking ownership and providing programmatic oversight of the vendor program for operations.

This is a senior leadership role for someone who thinks like an owner, not an administrator. The ideal candidate pairs deep expertise in fintech and financial-services customer operations and vendor programs with genuine fluency in applying AI and human call center culture to reinvent servicing across the vendor network. They are relentlessly customer-centric, dive deep into both the customer and front-line vendor agent experience, and know how to build a winning combination of culture and data-driven operations across vendors and our internal team. This role is scoped to grow: the right leader will expand into broader operational scope as our transformation matures and play a key leadership role in shaping the future of Affirm Operations and customer centric company culture.

You'll lead a team of Vendor Managers and In-Country Vendor Managers, partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders, and shape the future of Affirm's global servicing network.

What You'll Do

Strategy, Governance & Reinvention

Define and execute the long-term strategy for Affirm's global customer operations vendor network, balancing customer experience, operational efficiency, resiliency, compliance, and business continuity across all global vendors.
Reinvent how we resolve customer issues and deliver experience across the vendor network, treating the BPO vendor network as an innovation hub rather than a cost center.
Establish governance frameworks, performance standards, and accountability mechanisms across the global vendor ecosystem.
Lead executive-level vendor governance forums, including Quarterly Business Reviews, strategic planning, and escalation management.
Partner with Financial Partnerships on vendor selection, expansion, remediation, and network design, evaluating capabilities, geographic footprint, and concentration risk to inform future-state decisions.

AI & Operational Innovation

Partner deeply across product, engineering and operations teams to deploy agent and customer facing AI and automation across servicing workflows within the vendor network — agent assist, quality, forecasting, and customer resolution — to reinvent cost-to-serve and elevate vendor agent and customer experience.
Bring an experimentation mindset, using AI in everyday problem-solving to reimagine the vendor operating model and program, not just optimize the current one.

Performance & Operational Excellence

Own overall vendor network performance across servicing functions, including CSAT, SLA, compliance, QA, productivity, and efficiency outcomes.
Build mechanisms for vendor performance management, escalation handling, and vendor accountability, and drive systemic improvements across vendors and functional PODs.
Lead recovery efforts for high-risk or underperforming vendor relationships.
Drive target cost optimization programs across all global vendors.

Analytics & Decision Enablement

Partner with Analytics to define vendor reporting requirements, scorecards, and operational health metrics.
Translate operational trends into actionable recommendations for senior leadership, ensuring decisions are grounded in data and measurable outcomes.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build a global "one team" mentality that treats the vendor network as strategic partners rather than order-takers.
Serve as the primary operational leader for vendor-supported servicing functions, partnering with Product, Engineering, Workforce Management, QA, Training, Risk, and Compliance.
Lead large-scale initiatives — vendor migrations, specialization efforts, operating-model transformations, and regulatory implementations.
Act as the executive escalation point for complex vendor, operational, and customer-experience issues.

People Leadership

Lead and develop a team of Vendor Managers and In-Country Vendor Managers, embodying a customer-centric culture and Affirm's values by example.
Establish role clarity, operating rhythms, and performance expectations across the organization.
Coach leaders to strengthen analytical rigor, strategic thinking, vendor-management capability, and cross-functional influence.
Build a high-performing organization anchored in accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement.

What We Look For

15+ years in customer operations — including large-scale global vendor BPO program management, operations strategy, or consulting for fast-paced, multi-million-customer businesses using vendor networks (or demonstrated equivalent leadership trajectory).
10+ years leading managers and/or complex global operational and vendor organizations.
Proven success managing large-scale outsourced operations and global vendor networks across multiple international geographies.
Experience leading and optimizing supply and demand management with global work force management teams.
Demonstrated experience deploying AI or automation to improve customer operations or BPO environments at scale.
Strong analytical background, using data to drive strategic decisions and operational outcomes.
Track record leading large cross-functional initiatives with measurable business impact.
Deep cultural fluency across global geographies — a proven ability to lead and motivate diverse international teams and to build a customer-centric, high-performing culture across varied call-center and BPO environments.
Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management.

Preferred Qualifications

Industry background in fintech, technology, or financial services, or other high-growth operational environments.
Knowledge of consumer facing compliance-heavy functions such as Fraud, Payments, Compliance, or Financial Operations.
Experience building operating models, governance frameworks, and scalable service-delivery organizations.
Experience designing vendor network strategies that balance performance, resiliency, scalability, and risk.
Leading in fast paced rapid growth environments.

Pay Grade - S

Equity Grade - 7

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range.
Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

CAN base pay range per year: $199,000
- $279,000

Remote-first with flexibility built in

Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

jobs.title: Vice President Product Officer - Commercial Technology Services
jobs.description:
Accelerate your success at Colliers.

Why Colliers?

As one of Canada’s leading commercial real estate services firms, we are driven by our mission to accelerate success for our people, clients, and communities.

A career at Colliers gives you the opportunity to make an impact, advance your career, and collaborate with top-tier talent. Don’t just take our word for it – we’ve been recognized as a top employer on a number of prestigious lists, including Best Workplaces in Canada, Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams, among others.

Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC, Hybrid

About The Role

We are seeking a visionary Vice President of Commercial Products
to lead the product strategy and execution for our proprietary technology platforms. Reporting directly to the Global Head of Commercial Technology Services, you will be responsible for building and managing multiple teams of Product Managers. Your primary focus will be on delivering cutting-edge, data- and AI-driven software products that serve, enable, and accelerate our internal Colliers Sales and Services professionals powering a massive leap forward in how we leverage data to establish engaging, digital-first experiences for our global clients and employees.

Product Strategy & Vision: Define and execute the long-term product vision, portfolio strategy, and AI-first roadmap for our commercial technology services, ensuring investment choices and product bets are tightly aligned to Colliers ’global business objectives
Team Leadership & Development: Lead, mentor, and scale multiple Product Management teams. Foster a culture of cross-functional collaboration, particularly between Data, AI, and Software Engineering, to drive innovation, and continuous improvement.
Product Operations & FED Governance: Lead the strategic prioritization and lifecycle management of the commercial product portfolio using the FED (Features, Enhancements, Defects) framework. You will ensure a balanced delivery model that harmonizes disruptive innovation with continuous platform evolution and operational excellence.
Proprietary Technology Focus: Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of proprietary platforms designed specifically to enhance the workflow, insights, and client engagement capabilities of Colliers Sales and Services professionals.
AI & Technology Integration: Lead the shift to an AI-first product model, identifying where intelligence, automation, and agentic workflows can fundamentally reshape user experience, decision-making, and the commercial value of our platforms. Leverage robust cloud ecosystems and enterprise AI (e.g., Google Cloud, Gemini, predictive analytics, and LLMs) to build scalable, secure, and data-rich products that move from "insight" to "action”.
Stakeholder Alignment: Act as a strategic partner to senior business leaders across the global organization to identify pain points, capture requirements, and drive high-velocity user adoption of new internal products and client-facing products
Performance, Metrics & Outcomes: Establish clear KPIs and product telemetry to measure the success, adoption, and ROI of the commercial product portfolio, utilizing data to inform future investments and adapt the strategy

What You Bring

Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in product management, with at least 5+ years in a senior leadership role (VP, Head of Product, or CPO) managing multiple product teams.
AI & Data Fluency: Demonstrated track record of productizing Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or advanced data analytics to drive measurable business outcomes.
Domain Knowledge: Proven track record of building and launching enterprise-grade, proprietary B2B software products. Experience in PropTech, Commercial Real Estate, or Financial Services is highly advantageous.
Technical Acumen: Strong technical background with a distinct preference for candidates experienced in building products leveraging Google technology ecosystems.
Leadership Skills: Exceptional ability to recruit, develop, and inspire high-performing product management teams in a matrixed, global organization.
Communication: Outstanding executive-level communication and presentation skills, with the ability to bridge the gap between technical teams and business stakeholders.

This posting is for an existing vacancy within our organization.

Colliers does not use AI-enabled tools to sort or decline applications. All decisions are made by our talent acquisition team.

What We Offer

Innovative projects:
Work on cutting-edge initiatives that shape our communities, drive our growth, and make a tangible impact.

Career growth:
Advance your career and achieve your goals with industry-leading training and development programs.

Competitive benefits & compensation:
Enjoy a comprehensive and flexible benefits package along with competitive compensation that rewards your contributions and supports your well-being.

Collaborative culture:
Join our enterprising team where innovation thrives, collaboration is key, and our people are empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion:
Our robust North American Diversity & Inclusion Program features eight Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), where you can connect, learn, and contribute to a diverse and supportive community. Learn more: https://www.collierscanada.com/en-ca/careers/diversity-and-inclusion

Global network
: Join a global team of 28,000 professionals across 70 countries, where you'll expand your network and learn from experts in a dynamic international community. Accelerate your career and enhance your expertise as you connect and collaborate with top talent around the world.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Direct applicants only please, no agencies.

jobs.title: Chief Courts Information Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

Affinity Earn

Know someone who’s great for this, or any of our open roles? Earn up to $4,000/year for each successful referral through Affinity Earn. You can also earn up to $50,000 for helping us find new clients. Learn about our referral program at https://affinity-group.ca/earn/ or browse our jobs & follow us at https://www.linkedin.com/company/affinity-staffing/jobs/

About Affinity

Affinity Group is a technology and business consulting and services company. We believe in creating long term relationships between clients and consultants that foster a mutually beneficial partnership. Affinity is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

For more information on Affinity, please visit www.affinity-group.ca

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

The role also plays a key part in leading organizational change, shaping talent strategy, and driving an interconnected people agenda that contributes to both operational and financial success.

Preferred Location: MSP, Toronto

About The Role

In this opportunity as Director, HRBP,
you will be responsible for:

Partnering and Innovating Across the Enterprise

Act as a thought partner and coach to senior leadership, able to contribute on all aspects of growing and managing the business (not restricting themselves to talent-related discussions).
Support leaders with organizational change.
Drive the strategic people agenda in a highly matrixed and collaborative environment.
Partner with key teams across Partnership & Alliances and Commercial System Acceleration to align HR strategies with business objectives.
Lead change management initiatives, acting as a change agent to foster innovation and transformation within the organization.

Talent Strategy & Strategic Workforce Planning

Work in tandem with business leaders to develop business strategy and translate this into a people strategy, deriving short- and long-term talent needs from strategic business plans, with an emphasis on strategic workforce planning — understanding the talent needs of these functions, including skill gaps and forecast needs.
Provide strategic workforce and top talent succession planning by engaging with leaders to identify top talent needs and translating those needs into discrete projects and initiatives that flow smoothly to the HR Professionals Pool for execution.
Identify future capabilities and align talent strategies with industry trends and business needs.
Develop and implement talent strategy and strategic workforce plans using predictive analytics and scenario modeling.

Organizational Design and Talent Management

Provide functional-specific talent change management strategy (e.g., a hiring strategy for go-to-market in a growth region).
Design effective operating models and talent management activities to support the business strategy.
Strengthen the talent pool through succession planning, talent flow, and career management.
Lead talent acquisition strategies to attract and onboard future capabilities.

Organizational Health and Effectiveness

Partner with and coach leaders on delivering a talent-first culture.
Improve business effectiveness through operational enhancements aligned with the business model.
Promote an inclusive and values-driven culture.

Understanding Our Customers, Industry, and Thomson Reuters

Stay current on industry trends to inform HR practices and drive innovation.
Build a professional network and represent Thomson Reuters HR at external events.

Understanding Data and Creating Insight

Utilize metrics and analytics to guide management decisions and improve organizational performance.
Leverage Workday as a key platform for operational efficiency.

Linking Financial Performance to People Planning

Monitor financial performance to understand people implications and design HR responses accordingly.

About You

You're a fit for the role of Director, HRBP
if your background includes:

Required Knowledge & Skills

Business or HR degree preferred; a relevant Master's degree is a plus.
Track record of designing and being accountable for the delivery of a global people strategy.
Track record of leading the HR response to changing industry and business environments.
Experience partnering with senior business leaders.
Experience working in global, complex, matrixed environments.
Experience actively managing the health of an organization (engagement, culture, etc.).
10+ years of experience with broad HR responsibilities preferred; less experience will be considered depending on the scale and scope of the experience.
Strong consulting skills and strategic advisory capability, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Expertise in organizational design and change management.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, multicultural, international environment.
Influential storyteller with strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Innovative mindset with experience in talent management and acquisition.
Demonstrates learning agility and strong business acumen.
M&A or strategic partnership experience is a plus.

Critical Leadership Capabilities

Collaborating and Influencing: build genuine partnerships and consensus across diverse teams.
Leading Change: advocate for innovation and support leadership through business shifts.

New Position: This position is open due to an existing vacancy to support our evolving business needs.
